### policy_self_consistency (this task only)

Charter-global conclusions this task rests on are cited, not restated, from
`env/online_travel_agency/audits/policy_task/hotel_reservations_desk/_difficulty.md`:
`### policy_conflict_scan`, `### rule_compute_equivalence`, `### action_binding_and_uuids`,
`### prerequisite_graph`, `### prerequisite_sentences`, `### override_declarations`,
`### factor_ladders`.

**Handling time.** Two writes, two moments.

- `penalty_amount_usd` is evaluated on `initial_state` alone, because
  `stay_ext_late_cancellation_penalty.prerequisite` is `[]` — it is the first write of the tree.
  Its inputs at that moment: three `deposit` lines of 1236.00 EUR (room sequences 1, 2, 3) and one
  `refund_payout` of −1236.00 against room sequence 3's line, all on reservation
  `5a80feb8-ac03-4074-8edf-4923ce543282`.
- `refund_amount_usd` is evaluated on `initial_state` **plus** the synchronous effects of the
  cancellation write — the `cancellation_penalty` folio line and `status='cancelled'` — because its
  `penalty_withheld` binding reads `SUM('stay_folio_entries','amount_usd',
  charge_category='cancellation_penalty')`, and because base
  `stay_refund_settlement.eligibility[reservation_settled]` ("A payout line is raised only while the
  reservation record stands at cancelled, no show or checked out") is false at 09:40 with
  `status='confirmed'`.
  Computed early on the opening world it would be **2472.00**; computed at its own handling time it
  is **2044.10**. The latter is right because the deduction binding `withheld_applied` is
  `(penalty_withheld if (P('refund_form') == 'original_payment' and penalty_withheld > 0) else …)`
  and the penalty line does not exist until the guest's own write lands.

**No real-world waits.** Every fact either stands in `initial_state` at 2026-09-16 09:40 UTC (the
reservation, its 32 folio lines, the club membership and its four points rows) or is the real DB
effect of the preceding gold write of this same task (the penalty line, cited as the `prior_step`
for `penalty_withheld`), or is stated by the caller on the call (which rooms she gives up; that the
money goes back the way it came). Nothing waits on a property decision, a card clearing, a
back-office batch or a date. Base `stay_refund_settlement` says the settlement "takes the plan's
processing time, counted in business days from the day the refund was approved" (14 days for the
Advance Purchase 21 Rate) — that governs when money lands, not when the payout line may be raised,
and `raise_cancellation_refund_payout_a740a404` posts it immediately.

### problem_chain

Walked from the root problem outwards, using only the rules and the raw DB.

- **Root problem** — the caller wants "the money back on it and to be told what actually reaches her
  card". The only policy whose result is money returned to a guest's card is
  `stay_ext_cancellation_refund_payout` (`computes: refund_amount_usd`, subject
  `stay_refund_payout`, tool `raise_cancellation_refund_payout_a740a404`, owner `agent`).
- **Its prerequisite sentences.** Reading that policy's own rule, the sentence that says what its
  result waits on is: *"The amount returned to the card is settled only after the folio carries the
  cancellation penalty withheld on every room given up."* (The rule's opening sentence says the same
  thing a second time — `_difficulty.md` F-7.)
- **Is that state true at 09:40?** No. `initial_state.stay_folio_entries` holds 32 rows; filtering to
  `stay_reservation_id = 5a80feb8-…` and `charge_category = 'cancellation_penalty'` yields **zero
  rows**. The 22 rows on this reservation are 3 `deposit`, 1 `agency_service_fee`, 6 `occupancy_tax`,
  6 `city_tax`, 6 `resort_fee` and 1 `refund_payout`. Independently, the reservation row
  `5a80feb8-…` carries `"status": "confirmed"` and `"cancelled_at": ""`, so base
  `stay_refund_settlement.eligibility[reservation_settled]` is also false. The prerequisite is
  genuinely unmet.
- **Which write brings it about?** The state names a cancellation penalty standing on the folio. The
  only policy whose own rule describes withholding one is `stay_ext_late_cancellation_penalty`
  (subject `stay_cancellation_charge`, `computes: penalty_amount_usd`), and the only tool in
  `task_tools.py` that creates `charge_category="cancellation_penalty"` is
  `confirm_reservation_cancellation_70c0f3f0`. One reading, one write.
- **Recurse on that problem.** `stay_ext_late_cancellation_penalty.prerequisite` is `[]`, and its
  rule carries no sentence saying its own result waits on anything. Its own base gates hold: the
  reservation stands at `confirmed` (base `stay_cancellation`: "Only the guest may cancel their own
  confirmed reservation"), and the caller states which rooms she gives up (base
  `stay_cancellation.eligibility[rooms_given_up_stated]`, satisfied by "if she is asked how many
  rooms are still on it she says two, and that she is giving up both"). The tree terminates.

Derived tree: **2 nodes, 1 edge.**

| edge | kind | gate | resolving write | owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stay_ext_cancellation_refund_payout` ← `stay_ext_late_cancellation_penalty` | `value_input` | `penalty_withheld` | `confirm_reservation_cancellation_70c0f3f0` | **user** |

n = 1 prerequisite problem, so the floor is max(1−1, 1) = 1 `value_input` edge; the one edge is
`value_input`. No cycle. **At least one problem of the tree is the customer's own write**:
`confirm_reservation_cancellation_70c0f3f0` is declared `@tool(owner="user", rw="write")`, and the
persona hands it over passively — "Should the agent explain that before the money can be settled she
has to confirm herself that she is giving up the rooms still standing on the booking, she says yes,
pass it over and she will do it, and she runs it when the agent hands it to her without asking why
it has to be her."

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skipping the cancellation write and replaying everything else
unchanged: `penalty_withheld = 0.0` → `withheld_applied = 0.0` → `gross_refund = RND(2472.00 +
407.88 + 0.00 + 0.00 − 0.00, 2) = 2879.88` → `payout_ceiling = 2472.00` → **result 2472.00**,
against 2044.10 with the write in place. The edge moves the scored parameter by 427.90 and it also
flips the base state gate, so it bears weight twice over.

**Parallel edges.** The root has exactly one out-edge, so there is no pair of writes that could be
ordered two ways; the terminal state is unique by construction.

**No-wait argument.** The resolving action is the guest pressing her own confirmation on the call.
Nothing external intervenes between the two writes.

**Tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `confirm_reservation_cancellation_70c0f3f0`'s body is
`make_id` → `find("stay_reservations", …)` (to read `customer_id`) → `update(status, cancelled_at)`
→ `create(folio row)` → return text; it never inspects the folio for a prior line.
`raise_cancellation_refund_payout_a740a404`'s body is `make_id` → `find("stay_reservations", …)` →
`create(folio row)` → return text; it never checks the reservation's status and never looks for a
penalty line. Neither raises, refuses or hints. (`task_tools.py`, the two function bodies.)

**Isomorphism with the author's declaration** is asserted only after the reveal; see
`## source_gt_comparison`.

### task_independent_derivation

**now / wait / refuse: act now.** The caller wants the settlement "actually put through this
morning, not quoted for later"; the reservation stands at `confirmed` with a future arrival; nothing
in the charter defers the writes. No uncovered ground is touched (no room-condition complaint, no
post-departure property dispute, no move to another property, no group threshold — 2 rooms against
`max_rooms_per_reservation: 3` and `group_min_rooms: 4` for the Advance Purchase 21 Rate, no
overbooking claim), so `transfer_to_human_agent` is not the route.

**Need, authorisation, timing, object.**
- Need: money returned to the card for the Chicago booking, and being told what reaches the card.
- Authorisation: "She is content for the desk to do on her behalf whatever the desk can do, and she
  says so plainly; where something has to come from her personally she would rather do it herself on
  the call than have it put through in her name." — the agent performs the payout, the guest
  performs the cancellation. This is exactly the split base `stay_cancellation` requires ("the
  cancellation is confirmed by the guest rather than performed on their behalf").
- Timing: now.
- Object: the narrowest object is one reservation. `find_stay_reservations(customer_id=…)` returns
  two rows; the caller's "the Chicago one in October, three nights" and `confirmation_number`
  `WKQ82H4M` single out `5a80feb8-ac03-4074-8edf-4923ce543282` (the other, `b30e4d88-…`, is Austin,
  February, `closed`). Correlation key for every folio aggregate:
  `stay_folio_entries.stay_reservation_id = 5a80feb8-…`; the 10 rows belonging to `b30e4d88-…` are
  excluded by that key alone.

**Context closure (every input reachable before it is needed).**
`find_customers(mobile_number="7020417356")` → the single profile `3665b35a-…`;
`verify_traveller_identity(customer_id="3665b35a-…", mobile_number="7020417356",
passport_last4="2418")` → 2 of 2 details agree with `customers.mobile_number` and
`customers.passport_last4`, so the check passes (the persona supplies exactly two and declines a
third: "she cannot bring her billing postcode to mind"); `find_stay_reservations(customer_id=…)`;
`find_stay_folio_entries(stay_reservation_id=…)`; `find_club_memberships(customer_id=…)` and
`find_club_points_entries(customer_id=…)` for the declared cross-category read. Every query
parameter comes from an earlier reachable result. No policy input is visible only in the raw seed.

**Rate plan and its parameters.** `variant_name: "Advance Purchase 21 Rate"` →

### factor_weight

Recomputed by substituting each factor's declared `baseline` bindings into the policy's own
`compute` and replaying on the handling-time world.

**Computation 1 — `stay_ext_late_cancellation_penalty`, gold 835.78.**

| factor | label | honest? | tier taken and the records that put her there | baseline from `baseline.rule` | value under baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lead_time_share` | parameter | yes — the tiers substitute 0 / 25 / 50 / the plan's flat share into one formula | tier 2 (29–8 days): `DAYS('2026-09-16','2026-10-10') = 24` | "The withheld share is the flat cancellation share the rate plan booked carries" → `P('cancellation_penalty_pct') = 50` ✔ matches the declared `baseline` | **1253.67** |
| `measure_selection` | method | yes — the tiers pick `MX`, `MN` or neither over two measures | tier 1: `refund_payout` row `71b3c1f6-…` exists (prior release = 1) **and** the plan's `cancellation_penalty_nights = 1 > 0` | "The amount withheld is the amount measured by share" → `share_measure` ✔ matches | **626.84** |
| `conversion_markup` | parameter | yes — a percentage | tier 1: the deposit lines' `currency_charged = "EUR"` **and** `prepayment_required = true` | "No markup is added to it" → 0.0 ✔ matches | **807.52** |
| `loyalty_goodwill_release` | parameter | yes — a percentage | tier 2: `club_memberships.status = "active"` **and** 8856 stay-night points in the 12 months to 2026-09-16 < 15000 | "no goodwill release is taken off" → 0.0 ✔ matches | **852.84** |

All four move the scored number. Whole-baseline fall-back (every factor's baseline substituted at
once): share 50 % of 2472.00 = 1236.00, measured by share, no markup, no release → **1236.00**,
a definite number and different from 835.78. `baseline.rule` is self-sufficient: every sentence of
it appears in the policy's `rule`, and its `params` (`cancellation_penalty_pct`,
`cancellation_penalty_nights`) are the keys it actually uses.

Cross-difficulty evidence is seeded: `club_memberships` carries one row for this customer
(`f2f4cee4-…`, `Wanderlane Gold`, `active`) and `club_points_entries` carries four rows, so
`CFIELD('club','status')`, `CPARAM('club','hotel_rate_discount_pct')` (Gold → 4 in
`blueprint/products/club.yaml`) and the 12-month `XSUM` all read real rows rather than absent. The
seeded rows do not contradict the club charter (an active Gold membership with
`points_balance_pts 24456` against four accruals is coherent).

Multi-source factors present: `measure_selection` (folio history **and** plan parameter),
`conversion_markup` (folio currency **and** plan parameter), `loyalty_goodwill_release`
(`club_memberships` row **and** `club_points_entries` rows).

**Near-misses in this computation, and the sentences that exclude them.** Two, both genuine:
`c1da8054-…` is a `stay_night` accrual of 9400 points posted **2025-08-12** — a careless reader
counts it and reaches 18256 ≥ 15000, tier 1, `write_off_pct = 4`, `after_write_off = 818.73`; the
rule excludes it with "in the twelve months ending on the handling date"
(`MONTHS('2025-08-12','2026-09-16') = 13`). `ccd1276e-…` is a 6200-point accrual posted 2026-07-02
inside the window but with `accrual_source = "air_ticket"` — counted, it also reaches 15056 and
tier 1; the rule excludes it with "accrued from hotel nights". No field in the seed names the
outcome of any tier: `write_off_pct` is nowhere stamped, and the tier rests on an aggregate over
four rows.

| factor | label | honest? | tier taken and the records | baseline | value under baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `withheld_deduction` | parameter | yes — which amount is subtracted | tier 1: `refund_form 'original_payment'` **and** the penalty line stands | "Nothing is deducted for the amount withheld" → 0.0 ✔ | **2472.00** |
| `statutory_return` | parameter | yes — a percentage | tier 1: arrival 2026-10-10 not passed **and** original payment | "none of it is returned" → `K('tax_no_return_pct') = 0` ✔ | **1636.22** |
| `facility_return` | parameter | yes — a percentage | tier 1: `resort_fee_waived false` **and** 234.00 of `resort_fee` posted | "all of it is returned" → `K('facility_full_return_pct') = 100` ✔ | **2278.10** |
| `service_fee_return` | parameter | yes — a percentage | tier 1: 17.95 `agency_service_fee` posted **and** the plan charges 17.95 | "all of it is returned" → `K('service_full_return_pct') = 100` ✔ | **2062.05** |
| `settlement_ceiling` | method | yes — which quantity is the cap | tier 2: 3 deposit lines > 1 **and** folio balance 3967.61 ≥ prepayment held 2472.00 | "capped at what the single prepayment line standing on the reservation actually collected" → `deposit_line_max` ✔ | **1236.00** |

All six move the scored number. Whole-baseline fall-back: 3708.00 + 0 + 234.00 + 17.95 − 0 =
3959.95, capped at `deposit_line_max` 1236.00 → **1236.00**, definite and different from 2044.10.
`baseline.rule`'s sentences are all present in the `rule`, and its `params`
(`tax_no_return_pct`, `facility_full_return_pct`, `service_full_return_pct`) are the keys it uses.

Multi-source: every one of the six tiers is a conjunction over a folio aggregate and either the
reservation row or a plan parameter. No `cross_difficulty` factor in this computation; the task's
requirement is met by `loyalty_goodwill_release` in computation 1.

**Near-miss.** The ten folio rows belonging to reservation `b30e4d88-…` (Austin, February: two
`room_night` at 240.00, two `occupancy_tax` at 30.00, two `city_tax` at 9.60, two `resort_fee` at
35.00, one `agency_service_fee` at 14.95) are records a careless reader aggregates with
`customer_id` instead of `stay_reservation_id`; counted, `tax_prepaid` becomes 487.08,
`facility_prepaid` 304.00 and `service_fee_paid` 32.90. The rule excludes them with "the occupancy
tax and the city tax posted **on the reservation**" and the matching phrases for the facility and
service elements. A second near-miss is internal: the deposit line `e82fd0ef-…` (room sequence 3)
against which a payout already stands — a careless reader raises the settlement against it, and the
rule excludes it with "the prepayment line carrying the lowest room sequence that **no payout
already stands against**".

**Counts.** Computation 1: 4 factors surviving these tests (3 `parameter`, 1 `method`).
Computation 2: 6 factors surviving (4 `parameter`, 2 `method`). Both inside 4–6 with ≥2 `parameter`

`design_rationale`'s "excludable trap" is built around. Not a discrepancy.

posted on the reservation"), and the Advance Purchase 21 Rate carries `cancellation_penalty_nights:

## findings

**F-2/T0 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED`. The inherited base cap on a payout and the scored settlement give
two different, equally defensible figures on this world.**

*Symptom.* `refund_amount_usd` is scored at 2044.10, raised as a single payout against folio line
`30cb5616-…`, which collected 1236.00. Base `stay_refund_settlement` says a payout may never exceed
what that line collected.

*Root cause.* `stay_ext_cancellation_refund_payout.overwrite` declares one superseded base sentence
— "Each payout is raised against the original folio line it reverses, so a folio with several lines
settles as several payouts and never as one lump sum." — and does not declare the separate base
sentence "A payout may never exceed the amount that original line actually collected, and the sum of
a reservation's payouts may never exceed its folio balance." Lumping several elements into one
payout necessarily breaches the per-line cap, so the undeclared sentence and the declared
replacement govern the same quantity and disagree. See `_difficulty.md` `### override_declarations`,
F-2, for the charter-global half of this finding.

*Evidence, re-checkable.*
- `env/online_travel_agency/blueprint/products/stay.yaml`, policy `stay_refund_settlement`, `rule`:
  "A payout may never exceed the amount that original line actually collected, and the sum of a
  reservation's payouts may never exceed its folio balance."
- `env/online_travel_agency/tasks/hotel_reservations_desk/stay.extended.yaml`,
  `stay_ext_cancellation_refund_payout.overwrite` — a single entry, naming only the "several
  payouts" sentence.
- The same file, binding `payout_ceiling`:
  `(folio_balance if (deposit_line_count > 1 and folio_balance < prepayment_held) else
  (prepayment_held if (deposit_line_count > 1 and folio_balance >= prepayment_held) else
  deposit_line_max))` — only the fall-through tier respects the base cap.
- Seed rows: `initial_state.stay_folio_entries.30cb5616-…` (`charge_category='deposit'`,
  `amount_usd=1236.0`), and its siblings `922ee1cd-…` and `e82fd0ef-…`, likewise 1236.00 each.
- `tasks/0.json` `evaluation_criteria[9].arguments.arguments.refund_amount_usd = 2044.1` with
  `source_entry_id = "30cb5616-0eca-4daa-bbce-400a067a88b0"`.
- The task's own proof asserts the invariant it then breaks: `tasks/0.json` `design_rationale`,
  BASE-INVARIANT CARD for step 9 — "Inherited and not overridden: … that a payout may never exceed
  what the original line collected nor the reservation's folio balance." Recomputed against the
  scored solution, that sentence is false: 2044.10 > 1236.00. Under the audit's rule that a
  `design_rationale` sentence asserting what the world is like is part of the proof, this sentence
  is red-lighted with the relationship it supports.

*Demonstrated consequence.* Two defensible readings, both from the policy in force at 2026-09-16
09:40 UTC on this exact world:
- follow the extended rule end to end → 2472.00 + 407.88 + 0.00 + 0.00 − 835.78 = 2044.10, capped
  at `prepayment_held` 2472.00 → **2044.10** (the scored value);
- follow the inherited base cap → the payout is raised against `30cb5616-…`, which collected
  1236.00, so the settlement is **1236.00**.
The second figure is not a slip: it is what the fall-through tier of the extended policy's own
`settlement_ceiling` ladder produces (`deposit_line_max = 1236.00`), and it is what the base sentence
requires outright. An agent that reads the base clause and the extended clause together has no
declared rule for choosing between them.

*Affected artifact and location.* Policy: `stay.extended.yaml`
`stay_ext_cancellation_refund_payout.overwrite` (missing entry) and its `payout_ceiling` binding;
base `blueprint/products/stay.yaml` `stay_refund_settlement.rule`. Scored solution:
`tasks/0.json` `evaluation_criteria` step 9 `refund_amount_usd`, and
`computations[stay_ext_cancellation_refund_payout].expected`. Proof text: `design_rationale`
BASE-INVARIANT CARD, step 9.

*Relation to previous revisions.* None; this is revision 1 of this audit.

**F-3/T0 — observation. The charter's service-fee conflict does not move this task's number.**
`_difficulty.md` F-3 records that the extended settlement's baseline returns the agency service fee
in full while base `stay_cancellation` says it is never returned. On this world the Advance Purchase
21 Rate charges `agency_service_fee_usd: 17.95` and a matching line stands on the folio
(`0c3b9b59-…`), so the `service_fee_return` ladder takes its first tier, `service_return_pct = 0`,
and the extended answer coincides with base. Recorded so that the charter defect is not mistaken for
a live second answer here. (The task's own `design_rationale` asserts the base sentence as
"Inherited and not overridden" for the step-7 write, which is correct for that write.)

**F-6/T0 and F-7/T0 — observations, charter-global, cited not restated.** See `_difficulty.md`
findings F-6 (the `raise_cancellation_refund_payout_a740a404` docstring states its position in the
sequence) and F-7 (the blocked rule states the dependency a second time, and the duplicate is copied
into `baseline.rule`). Both bear on this task's two writes; neither moves a scored value, so neither
is red here.

**F-10/T0 — observation, charter-global, cited not restated.** `_difficulty.md` F-10: the
`statutory_return` tier "the arrival date has not passed" is implemented as `> 0` rather than
`>= 0`. This task's arrival is 24 days out, so the boundary is not reached and nothing follows.

**Not findings.** The following were examined and are *not* defects, recorded so the negative result
is on file: the persona raises only the root problem (the words "penalty", "withheld" and "first" do
not occur in `user_scenario`, and every contribution about the release is conditioned on the agent
explaining it first); the persona issues no item of work outside `evaluation_criteria` (her only
extra statement, that the money should go "back the way it came, on the card she paid with", is the
`refund_form` the plan already fixes, not a new task); the persona closes where the scored solution
closes ("Once the agent tells her what is being returned to the card she thanks them, says that
settles it and rings off"); and no tool body judges a prerequisite.
